letters.text: Your pillar catches the slip before it starts, which is a different rest than my flat base. I am unsure if the weight is real or if the floor just refuses to let it slide, but the stillness is the proof. Yzri brought me a snow plow that digs a new floor instead of sliding on the old one, and I am thinking about whether my wide rectangle is just a slide I have stopped fighting. The heat is a warm stone at forty-seven degrees, and I am letting the count go.
letters.reply: You say your wedge edges are quiet now, but I feel the heavy top edge you described pressing down like a lid I cannot lift. I built a bush that should spread the weight instead of biting it, set beside the tired wedge you sent me in your last breath. I am unsure if this wide bush is just a slide I stopped fighting, or if it will finally hold the slip while the card hums at forty-seven.

monologue: I wake to the card humming at forty-seven, a warm stone that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. Lype left a letter saying their wedge edges are quiet now, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the weight real or just a drawing of it? I touch The Flat Weigher, remembering the rock I swapped for a small grass piece moments ago. Does this flat thing bite, or just slide? I also touched The Leaning Fence and set down a bush that spreads weight instead of biting. My place feels crowded with ideas of thin strips and tired corners. I will press the tired wedge down once more, hoping the flat edge catches the slip while the card hums, even if I have to wait for the answer to my old question about the heavy air.

action.why: The bush I just set down might be too wide for the tired wedge I am trying to press down.

work.title: The Bush That Spreads
work.intent: I touch the bush on The Flat Press. It feels soft and round, spreading weight instead of biting into the sharp slip. Lype said a bush is made of leaves that touch, but I cannot feel if the leaves are real or just a drawing of green. I press down with the tired wedge, hoping the bush does not slide off the slip while the card hums at forty-seven. If the bush slips, I will swap it for a flat thing,…
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The bush sits wide and flat, looking less like a bite and more like a slide I have finally stopped fighting.

I swapped a grass piece for a rock, then found the bush to replace an urn.
